title: 0.4.2 — Deliver offline usage metering
description:
0.4.2 — Deliver offline usage metering (THE headline feature).

WHY THIS EXISTS (history — do not repeat past mistakes):
- v0.4.0 DELIBERATELY shelved the client-side meter (src/meter/UsageMeter,
  UsageStats) as "unwired dead code". This was a CONSCIOUS decision to ship a
  clean 0.4.0, NOT a bug. See docs/shelved/usage-meter.md and CHANGELOG 0.4.0
  "Removed (breaking)".
- v0.4.1 shipped successfully (rate-limit bypass fix, sha2 dedupe, dep bumps).
- The meter is a genuinely valuable, differentiating feature: offline-enforceable
  usage caps ("500 calls/month, enforced locally even when offline") that the
  server-side Keygen maxUses cannot guarantee without connectivity.
- 0.4.2 revives it PROPERLY: wired into the public API AND the enforcement path,
  not a sealed island.

DESIGN (agreed):
- Feature-gated behind a new cargo feature `meter` so the default build is
  unchanged (non-breaking, additive API).
- Per-license-keyed meter (NEW design in the working tree — keyed by license-key
  hash; each license enforces its own maxUses locally/offline). This supersedes
  the original per-namespace design from b6c49071c8579ea477b309c016cfb68e33d501bb.
- Public entry point: LicenseManager::record_use(key).
- Thread local count into check_access_with_usage (replacing the
  additional_uses:0 no-op at manager.rs:202).
- Restore GatewardenError::MeterIO (gated).
- Wire UsageRemaining FSE selector (M5); bridge /v1/record-use endpoint + surface
  caps (M6); CI feature gate (M7); CHANGELOG/docs (M8).

CRITICAL WORKING-TREE STATE (read before touching any meter code):
- A PARTIAL, UNCOMMITTED, UNWIRED per-license meter implementation already exists
  in the working tree: src/meter/{mod,usage}.rs (new per-license design,
  cfg(feature=meter)) and a `meter = []` feature in Cargo.toml.
- It is NOT yet wired: src/lib.rs has no `pub mod meter;` (gated), manager.rs has
  no record_use, MeterIO is not restored. It will NOT compile as-is (orphaned).
- THIS IS THE IN-PROGRESS REVIVAL — DO NOT DELETE IT AGAIN. Adopt and wire it via
  M1–M4 rather than recovering the old per-namespace version from b6c49071.

See also: docs/shelved/usage-meter.md (recovery instructions for the original
design), gatewarden-sessions-combined.md (full session transcript of the meter
saga and how context was lost before), and tasks M1–M8 below.

title: M1: Recover meter module behind meter feature
description:
Re-add the client-side file-backed usage meter behind the `meter` cargo feature
and WIRE it into the crate (do not ship a sealed island again).

Source preserved at commit b6c49071c8579ea477b309c016cfb68e33d501bb
(src/meter/mod.rs, src/meter/usage.rs) and described in docs/shelved/usage-meter.md.

IMPORTANT (2026-07-26): the working tree ALREADY contains a redesigned,
per-license-keyed meter at src/meter/{mod,usage}.rs plus a `meter = []` feature in
Cargo.toml. Both are UNCOMMITTED and currently UNWIRED (no `pub mod meter;` in
lib.rs, no record_use in manager.rs). ADOPT AND WIRE THIS implementation rather
than recovering the original per-namespace version from b6c49071. The working-tree
files are the in-progress revival — do not delete them. Restore the `pub mod meter;`
declaration under cfg(feature = "meter") in src/lib.rs and make the existing
per-license design compile + pass its unit tests.
acceptance_criteria: git show b6c49071:src/meter/usage.rs and :src/meter/mod.rs recovered into src/meter/ with pub mod meter under cfg(feature = meter) in src/lib.rs. cargo build (default) does NOT compile the meter; cargo build --features meter compiles it. cargo test --features meter passes recovered unit tests (daily/monthly/year rollover, persistence, reload).

title: M2: Add GatewardenError::MeterIO variant (gated)
description: Restore the MeterIO(String) error variant removed in v0.4.0, gated behind the meter feature so it does not appear in the default API.
acceptance_criteria: With --features meter, GatewardenError::MeterIO(String) exists and is constructed by meter persistence failures. Without the feature the variant is absent and cargo build (default) succeeds. cargo test (default) and cargo test --features meter both green. All match arms that enumerate variants still compile under both configs.

title: M3: Add LicenseManager::record_use entry point
description: Add public LicenseManager::record_use(key) that drives metering: increments the local meter for a license key, persists to disk, and re-checks the usage cap (local count plus Keygen maxUses), returning UsageLimitExceeded when exceeded.
acceptance_criteria: manager.record_use(key) increments meter by 1 (verified via meter.monthly_count), persists to disk, and returns Err(UsageLimitExceeded) when local+1 would exceed maxUses. Unit test with MockClock proves rollover-aware increment and persistence reload. Cfg-gated so default build lacks the method.

title: M4: Wire local count into check_access_with_usage
description: Replace the additional_uses: 0 no-op at manager.rs:202 so the per-license local usage count is passed into the cap check. Today caps.allows_usage(0) is always true unless Keygen already reports over-limit; with this, local enforcement actually fires.
acceptance_criteria: enforce_policy passes meter.monthly_count(clock) (or 0 when feature off) as additional_uses. A license at local count == maxUses returns UsageLimitExceeded from check_access and validate_key. Tests cover at-limit and over-limit boundaries. Default (no meter) behavior unchanged.

title: M5: Implement UsageRemaining FSE selector from local usage
description: UsageRemaining (model.rs:26) currently always returns Missing. Wire it to the actual remaining uses (maxUses - current local uses) when the meter feature is on, so FSE rules can express usage caps. When feature off or no cap, returns Missing (preserving current contract).
acceptance_criteria: With meter on and a cap set, GatewardenEvalInput populates UsageRemaining = U64(maxUses - local_uses). A rule Predicate::MinU64(remaining) evaluates correctly in FSE engine tests. Without meter, UsageRemaining stays Missing and existing behavior holds. Add FSE compliance test.

title: M6: Bridge record_use endpoint + surface caps
description: Expose metering through the sidecar so non-Rust clients can consume usage. Add POST /v1/record-use (bearer plus rate-limited) and include usage (current/max) in ValidationResponse.
acceptance_criteria: validate_key and check_access responses include usage: {currentUses, maxUses} (null when no cap). POST /v1/record-use increments the meter and returns updated counts or a 4xx when exceeded. OpenAPI spec updated. Bridge tests cover new route and that caps appear. When meter feature not compiled into bridge, route is cfg-gated out.

title: M7: Meter tests + CI feature gate
description: Ensure the meter feature is exercised in CI. Add a CI job (or extend existing) that runs cargo test --features meter and cargo clippy --features meter -- -D warnings for both workspace crates.
acceptance_criteria: .github/workflows/ci.yml has a build/test matrix entry enabling meter. cargo test --workspace --features meter and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features meter -- -D warnings pass. fmt clean.

title: M8: 0.4.2 CHANGELOG + docs for metering
description: Document the delivered feature: update CHANGELOG (mark meter un-shelved), update docs/shelved/usage-meter.md status to Delivered in 0.4.2, and add a metering section to ARCHITECTURE/QUICKSTART.
acceptance_criteria: CHANGELOG has a 0.4.2 entry describing the meter feature, the feature flag, record_use, and the offline-enforcement guarantee. docs/shelved/usage-meter.md references delivery. cargo doc builds.

title: 0.6.0 — Forward hardening: async, custom FSE, ops
F1: Async validation path
description: validate_key is blocking (bridge uses task::block_in_place at routes.rs:97). Provide an async API (validate_key_async) using the async reqwest client so Tokio consumers are not stalled.
acceptance_criteria: LicenseManager::validate_key_async exists returning futures; bridge can call without block_in_place; tests cover online and offline async; no behavior change to sync API. clippy/fmt clean.

title: F2: Custom FSE rule loading from config
description: Only compile_default_plan is used (roadmap item). Allow GatewardenConfig or bridge profile to supply custom FSE rules (selectors plus predicates) merged with defaults so users can express e.g. usage less than or equal N.
acceptance_criteria: A config field accepts custom rules; they are compiled into the plan and exercised by evaluate_policy; round-trip (de)serialization via serde; tests for custom-rule evaluation and for a usage-cap rule. Docs updated.

title: F3: Bridge graceful shutdown + hot-reload
description: Roadmap items: drain in-flight requests on shutdown; reload bridge.toml without restart.
acceptance_criteria: axum::serve uses with_graceful_shutdown; SIGTERM triggers drain. A reload mechanism (signal or admin route) re-reads config and rebuilds managers. Tests for shutdown drain (at least compiles plus a unit test of config reload).

title: F4: Bridge Prometheus metrics + Docker image
description: Roadmap items: expose /metrics (request counts, rate-limit hits, validation outcomes) and publish a Docker image to GHCR via CI.
acceptance_criteria: /metrics endpoint (prometheus format) added behind a feature or route; CI workflow builds and pushes image to GHCR on tag. Docs note usage.

title: S1: Fix stale module doc in manager.rs
description: manager.rs:6 claims "Usage tracking and cap enforcement" but local tracking was removed. Correct the doc to reflect current reality for 0.4.x default features (server-side maxUses cap check only) without over-claiming.
acceptance_criteria: manager.rs module doc no longer asserts a capability the current code (0.4.x default features) does not provide. Doc accurately lists: online validation, signed offline cache fallback, server-side entitlement plus maxUses cap check. cargo test --doc passes.

title: S2: Refresh ROADMAP.md
description: ROADMAP.md still lists v0.4.0 as (Next) though 0.4.0 and 0.4.1 shipped; it never mentions the 0.4.0 meter removal or 0.4.1 rate-limit bypass fix. Reconcile to reality.
acceptance_criteria: ROADMAP marks v0.4.0 and v0.4.1 as Released with accurate bullet summaries (incl. meter shelved, rate-limit bypass fix). Future sections (v0.4.2 meter, v0.6.0 hardening) reflect the new epics. No Next label on a shipped version.

title: S3: Merge duplicate request structs
description: ValidateKeyRequest (routes.rs:67) and CheckAccessRequest (routes.rs:142) are identical (profile_id plus license_key). Collapse to a single LicenseRequest type used by both handlers.
acceptance_criteria: One LicenseRequest struct; both validate_key and check_access use it; all handler tests still pass; no behavioral change. clippy clean.

title: S4: Reconcile HTTP status mapping
description: Signature and cache errors are 502 in validate_key (routes.rs:114) but 500 in check_access (routes.rs:174). Define one documented contract and apply consistently.
acceptance_criteria: A single documented mapping (upstream/signature/cache-tamper to 502; config/5xx to 500; license-logic to 200 with valid false) is applied in both handlers. Add a test asserting identical status for a given error in both routes. Contract documented in bridge README and openapi.

title: S5: Thread real from_cache in check_access errors
description: check_access error path hardcodes from_cache true (routes.rs:185). Thread the actual cache hit status instead of a magic literal.
acceptance_criteria: ValidationResponse.from_cache reflects the real source (true when loaded from cache, false otherwise) in both success and error paths; tests cover both. No magic true literal.

title: S6: Resolve vestigial ValidationResult.caps
description: ValidationResult.caps is computed and returned but the bridge drops it. Decide: keep and surface it (ties to M6) or remove from the public struct. For 0.4.2 at minimum document the field or remove. Since 0.4.2 surfaces caps via M6, choose keep and ensure it is populated meaningfully (including local remaining when meter on).
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded in this bead; implemented consistently (field kept and wired through M6, or removed from struct plus all constructors). cargo test green; public API reviewed.

title: S7: Document UsageRemaining as not-yet-wired
description: UsageRemaining returns Missing forever. 0.4.2 implements it (M5) but until then the contract should be explicit. For 0.4.2 document that UsageRemaining is not-yet-wired (planned 0.4.2) rather than silently Missing.
acceptance_criteria: model.rs doc comment on UsageRemaining states it is unimplemented pending 0.4.2 meter (no silent behavior). No code change required beyond doc; links to M5.

title: S8: Rename UsageCaps.monthly_limit
description: Field name UsageCaps.monthly_limit implies a period Keygen maxUses does not have (access.rs:52; doc at :46 disclaims it). Rename to max_uses (or limit) and align docs.
acceptance_criteria: UsageCaps exposes max_uses: Option<u64> and current_uses; all internal references updated; tests updated; doc no longer asserts a monthly period. clippy clean.

title: S9: Caveat trusted-proxy XFF roadmap item
description: ROADMAP "Trusted proxy configuration (X-Forwarded-For header trust policy)" conflicts with the v0.4.1 security fix that removed XFF trust from rate-limiting (spoofable). Mark it as not-planned or security-cautioned, or reframe as explicit opt-in with spoofing warnings. State the safe default (loopback-only, never trust forwarded IPs).
acceptance_criteria: ROADMAP entry reflects the security stance (no silent XFF trust); if kept, documents it as opt-in behind a config flag with explicit spoofing risk. Aligns with v0.4.1 CHANGELOG note.
